items.name: Ṱhangule
items.flag: Requires correct Unicode Ṱ (T with line below); plain 'Th' would be a different letter. Unrelated to Ṱhafamuhwe despite shared prefix.

items.name: Shundunthule
items.flag: Long, easily misspelled (Shundunthule vs Shundunthule variants); less commonly seen than other names. Some sources vary the spelling.

items.name: Ṱhafamuhwe
items.flag: Shares Ṱha- prefix with Ṱhangule (Aug); confusable by short form if diacritic is dropped. Requires Ṱ.

items.name: Fulwi
items.flag: Easily confused with Fulwana (July); short form 'Fulw' collides with Fulwana's stem. Also evokes winter/cold, so could be read as a season.

items.name: Nyendavhusiku
items.flag: Long name, easily misspelled; some sources spell it differently. Low-frequency form.

items.name: Tshimedzi
items.flag: Similar ending to Khubvumedzi (Sept); confusable if abbreviated or skimmed.

items.name: Ḽara
items.flag: Requires correct Unicode Ḽ (L with circumflex below); a plain 'Lara' would look like a personal name. Short and easily confused.

items.name: Fulwana
items.flag: Diminutive of Fulwi; confusable with Fulwi (June). Short form 'Fwan' is not the first four letters (those would collide with Fulwi), so it is a deliberate disambiguation.

items.name: Luhuhi
items.flag: Less commonly attested; some sources differ on the Feb/March assignment.

items.name: Lambamai
items.flag: Looks like a loan from 'Lamba' plus 'Mai' (May); a reader might wrongly map it to May. It is April.

items.name: Khubvumedzi
items.flag: Similar ending to Tshimedzi (Oct); confusable if abbreviated.

summary: Machine-generated review from model knowledge only, not a fluent-speaker or native-linguist approval. All 12 names map to distinct months, consistent with the standard South African Tshivenda calendar (Phando=Jan ... Nyendavhusiku=Dec). No outright misspellings found, and none look like non-South-African-only forms. Main risks: (1) Fulwi (Jun) vs Fulwana (Jul) near-collision, with Fulwi also suggesting a winter season; (2) Tshimedzi vs Khubvumedzi share an ending; (3) Ṱhangule vs Ṱhafamuhwe share a prefix and depend on the Ṱ diacritic, as does Ḽara on Ḽ; (4) Lambamai superficially resembles 'May' but is April. The less common names (Shundunthule, Luhuhi, Nyendavhusiku, Ḽara) have medium confidence and should get a native-speaker check.
